subject: Shoulder prewarm, crediting and fallback procedure for Meridian Data dedicated pools

Subject: Dedicated pool: shoulder prewarm & burst crediting question

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough. As we map production traffic for Q3, we have sustained baseline on a small fraction of requests but several predictable spikes tied to nightly batch jobs and end-of-month analytics. Procurement asked me to clarify two things before we sign: 1) how prewarm windows and shoulder capacity will be handled operationally (we want cold-starts avoided during the 02:00-04:00 PST window), and 2) how Redwood will credit us if we need sustained headroom above the committed baseline during a launch.

I attached a short Q3 traffic forecast. Can you share an explicit playbook for prewarm windows, the fallback behavior if dedicated capacity is saturated, and an example crediting calculation? We want this stitched into the SLA addendum.

Best,
Alice

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the forecast and the clear ask. We ran an initial read of the file and sketched a practical runbook. High-level summary below; attaching the PDF runbook for detail. Happy to sync but want to capture the proposal in thread first so procurement has a written record.

Proposal (summary):
- Baseline reservation: match committed slab (example: 40 A100 equivalent GPUs).
- Shoulder prewarm: schedule an automated prewarm window 01:30–02:15 PST with an aggressive prefix pre-warm (KV warmers + async prefetch). We recommend a 45-minute prewarm ahead of your 02:00 peak to ensure KV/cache hits.
- Ephemeral burst pool: allow up to a 60-GPU ephemeral pool for short-term spikes; bursts beyond that trigger graceful degradation to a lower-capacity model variant (quantized fallback).
- Crediting model: crediting is based on headroom minutes consumed above baseline over the billing month. Example calculation in attached SLA doc (SLA-addendum-prewarm-crediting.docx).

Rishi and Ben — can you confirm the numbers below are feasible operationally? Also listing a few items I want you to check: backlog prefill impact on cold starts, KV retention window required for the prewarm to be effective, and any necessary runbook ops steps for on-call.

Thanks,
Mina
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Mina / team — quick ops read: the approach is solid; a few operational caveats and suggested changes.

1) Prewarm mechanics
- For your workload shape, the prewarm should prime both KV cache and token-prefix caches. We recommend a two-stage prewarm: 30 minutes of async KV priming (background replay of representative prompts) followed by a 10-minute hot-path burst that routes a small fraction of live traffic to the warmed slab (smoke test). That gives us an 40-minute effective warm window.

2) Ephemeral burst sizing & soft caps
- Baseline: 40 GPUs (committed).
- Shoulder buffer (pre-committed reserve for scheduled windows): +20 GPUs (total 60) available on scheduled prewarm windows. These are reserved and billed at reduced shoulder rate when consumed during the scheduled window.
- Ephemeral pool (unscheduled spikes): additional 30 GPUs on best-effort. If ephemeral pool >30 GPUs, trigger model-fallback to quantized variant and enqueue non-critical jobs (batch analytics) into a delayed queue.

3) Failover behavior
- If both reserved shoulder and ephemeral pool are saturated, traffic is routed to a reduced-throughput model variant (4-bit quantized) and a short 429-based backpressure path is signaled to clients with Retry-After headers. We will provide example fallback hooks for your engineers.

4) Metrics & SLIs
- We will emit shoulder-reserve-utilization, ephemeral-burst-utilization, cold-start-rate, prefix-cache-hit-rate. Suggest a 99th-percentile tail-latency SLO for the baseline slab and a separate SLO for shoulder window requests.

I will attach an ops checklist in the shared drive; Mina — if you approve these numbers I will schedule a dry-run prewarm during the next maintenance window.

— Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-ops-prewarm-checklist.md (attached to Drive link)

Alice / Meridian procurement —

Thanks for the ask. Commercial note on crediting and the SLA addendum: we typically offer two options for shoulder/ephemeral crediting tied to reserved capacity:

A) Monthly true-up credits: any minutes of headroom consumed above baseline during scheduled prewarm windows are credited at a blended rate (example: 50% of token/unit list price) as a one-line true-up on the following invoice. This is simplest for procurement.

B) Pre-bought shoulder credits: Meridian can pre-purchase a shoulder credit allocation (blocks of GPU-hours) at a discounted rate. Unused credits roll forward for up to 2 billing cycles.

For the SLA language, we will add explicit notification windows: 48-hour scheduled prewarm notice for reserved shoulder, plus an on-call contact for emergency prewarms. DocuSign link for the SLA-addendum is below; once procurement confirms option A vs B we will finalize the quantity and pricing in the DocuSign.

Next steps I propose:
- Meridian picks crediting option (A or B)
- Redwood schedules a dry-run prewarm during a mutually available maintenance window (we recommend Aug 19–21)
- Sign SLA addendum (DocuSign)

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Scheduled shoulder reserve: +20 GPUs available during 01:30–02:30 PST prewarm windows (billed at shoulder rate).
- Ephemeral best-effort pool: +30 GPUs for unscheduled spikes; >30 triggers model fallback to quantized variant and queueing for non-critical jobs.
- Prewarm cadence: two-stage prewarm (30m KV priming + 10m hot-path smoke) starting 01:15 to reach full warm by 01:55.
- Crediting: Meridian chooses Option A (monthly true-up credits) per Ben's doc; example calculation included in SLA (DocuSign).
